name: American Revolution
hook: Lexington, Yorktown, Lafayette and the times that try men's souls: the war in six facts.

facts.label: Lexington and Concord
facts.statement: The Revolutionary War began at Lexington and Concord in April 1775; John Nixon commanded minutemen at that first battle.

facts.label: Yorktown
facts.statement: The 1781 siege of Yorktown ended the war; Alexander Hamilton led an attack there, and the same Virginia port fell again in 1862.

facts.label: the Marquis de Lafayette
facts.statement: The Marquis de Lafayette was a teenage French aristocrat who became a Continental Army major general; at 72 he helped lead France's 1830 July Revolution.

facts.label: Thomas Paine
facts.statement: Thomas Paine wrote "These are the times that try men's souls" and edited Pennsylvania Magazine, which helped bring on the war.

facts.label: John Paul Jones
facts.statement: Congress gave John Paul Jones a gold medal in 1787 for his naval leadership, and in 1788 he accepted a rear admiral's post in the Russian navy.

facts.label: Paul Revere
facts.statement: Paul Revere was a silversmith who made copper fittings for Old Ironsides and was court-martialed as a lieutenant colonel long after his famous ride.

facts.label: "Mad Anthony" Wayne
facts.statement: Boldness in battle earned General Anthony Wayne the nickname "Mad Anthony"; after the war he served a year in Congress.
